- [ ] **Step 3: Write the code,** `scripts/plaud_spike.py`: the guard, the spike folder, and each spike's steps and print list from spec §18, S1 to S12. S2 and S4 POST to the token URL (the only POSTs, on purpose, at Dan's word); S10 and S11's raw GETs read the header names and the `Range` answer the client keeps to itself. The guard refuses before any call when the archive can't say what is private (the council's S3), adds the deployment's patterns and word and the enforced words, and checks the envelope's own title before any block or download (S7); `--own-clip` is refused for a recording in the archive (S8); any exception prints its class only (S9); a refresh sends the token file's `client_id`, and a refusal's advice depends on its OAuth error code (G3); S9 takes its clip by the 8-hex name it printed (G4).

```python
"""The Plaud spikes (stage 2b spec §18): supervised test plans, each run with Dan in a session.

    uv run python scripts/plaud_spike.py <spike> [--home DIR] [--production-config FILE]
        [--token-file FILE] [--id ID]... [--token-url URL] [--own-clip]

It imports `recordings`, so it runs in the workspace, with no PEP 723 block (2b phase 1 plan,
decision 24). Never in CI and never by an agent: only in Dan's sessions A (s1, s2, s4, s3), B (s5,
s7, s8, s10, s12, s11) and C (s9), from a clone of its own, as runbook section 1c says. Its tests
run it against fakes.

**The guard** is built before any Plaud call, and refuses the whole spike (exit 78) when it can't
be sure: a consent stop (the list is read fail-closed); an `[archive] path` that holds no
`archive.json`, or an archive with no recordings or with recordings it can't read (it couldn't
tell which are private); and the deployment's `config.toml` (`--production-config`, by default
`$REPO_DIR/config.toml`) unreadable. Its keep-out words are the session config's, the
deployment's, every word the worker has enforced (`state.db`, when `[state] path` is set) and the
default; its patterns are the session config's and the deployment's, so a hand copy that drifted
only adds. A spike that fetches `files/{id}` or downloads audio refuses any consent-listed ID, any
recording tagged private in the archive, any title a keep-out word matches (S9's own clip aside:
`--own-clip`, for a clip that isn't in the archive), and any title an auto-private pattern
matches, the own clip included (decision 24). A row with no title can't be checked, so it is
refused as well. The envelope's own title is checked again before any block or download (§11.5).
Every spike ends by printing how many it refused, by reason.

**What it prints** is each spike's §18 print list: counts, yes or no, times, status codes, field
names and `short()` prefixes (8 hex of a SHA-256). Never a token, a title, transcript text or a
whole Plaud ID. An error line names an exception's class, never its text, whatever the exception.

**The spike folder** is `$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike`, mode 0700, outside the archive, the state folder,
the index, `/plaud` and every backup path. The session's sign-in (a temporary HOME, `--token-file`)
lives in it, and so does anything a spike downloads, deleted at once, and S9's record of its clip.
Dan deletes the folder at the end of the session (runbook 1c). A spike never refreshes the sign-in
behind Dan's back: S2 and S4 refresh on purpose, at the token URL Dan finds in the vendor CLI's own
refresh before session A (`--token-url`, https only).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import base64
import collections
import json
import os
import re
import sqlite3
import stat
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import tomllib
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from recordings.archive import Archive, sha256_file
from recordings.config import Config, ConfigError, load_config
from recordings.ids import ID_RE
from recordings.models import Recording, is_private
from recordings.plaud.client import (
    API_BASE,
    FILE_PATH,
    LIST_PATH,
    PAGE_SIZE,
    Listed,
    PlaudAuthError,
    PlaudClient,
    PlaudError,
    check_api_base,
    check_link,
    id_hash,
)
from recordings.plaud.consent import ConsentListError, consent_list_path
from recordings.plaud.keepout import DEFAULT_WORD, fold, keep_out_match, read_consent, valid_word
from recordings.plaud.normalise import part_hashes, transcript_rows
from recordings.plaud.reconcile import matches_auto_private, patterns_from_config
from recordings.refs import canonical_plaud_id
from recordings.sentinel import SentinelError, read_sentinel
from recordings.state import State

SPIKES = ("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4", "s5", "s7", "s8", "s9", "s10", "s11", "s12")
REASONS = ("consent", "private", "keep-out", "pattern")
EXIT_REFUSED = 78
PLAUD_MOUNT = Path("/plaud")
PAUSE = 60.0  # S5 and S8: "a minute apart"
MOMENT = 5.0  # S9: "a moment apart"
PAGE_CAP = 500  # §11.2: a listing that reaches it is bad
TIMEOUT = 60.0
SIZES = (5, 20, 50, 100, 500)  # S5's page sizes
_CODE_CHARS = frozenset("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz_")
_SHORT = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{8}")  # an ID as this script prints it (S9's --id may be one)
ENFORCED_WORDS = "keep_out_words"  # plaud_state's key for the words the worker enforced (Task 6)
_LIST_KEYS = ("data", "data_list", "files", "items", "list")
sleep = time.sleep  # the tests replace it: a spike's pauses are real only in Dan's sessions


class SpikeRefused(Exception):
    """A fixed phrase: main() prints it and exits 78."""


@dataclass
class Guard:
    consent: frozenset[str]  # canonical IDs; a consent stop raises SpikeRefused before any call
    private_ids: frozenset[str]  # canonical Plaud IDs of archive recordings tagged private
    here: frozenset[str]  # canonical Plaud IDs of every recording in the archive
    words: tuple[str, ...]
    patterns: tuple[str, ...]
    refused: collections.Counter[str] = field(default_factory=collections.Counter)

    def allows(self, plaud_id: str, title: str | None, *, own_clip: bool = False) -> bool:
        """Whether a spike may fetch or download this recording. `own_clip` (S9's clip) skips the
        keep-out check, and nothing else."""
        canonical = canonical_plaud_id(plaud_id)
        if canonical in self.consent:
            reason = "consent"
        elif canonical in self.private_ids:
            reason = "private"
        elif title is None:
            reason = "pattern"  # no title to check: refused, the safe way
        elif not own_clip and keep_out_match(title, self.words):
            reason = "keep-out"
        elif matches_auto_private([title, fold(title)], self.patterns):
            reason = "pattern"
        else:
            return True
        self.refused[reason] += 1
        return False

    def report(self) -> str:
        total = sum(self.refused.values())
        if not total:
            return "refused: 0"
        parts = ", ".join(f"{r} {self.refused[r]}" for r in REASONS if self.refused[r])
        return f"refused: {total} ({parts})"


def short(value: str) -> str:
    """8 hex of the SHA-256: the only form an ID, or any other value, is printed in. A Plaud ID is
    hashed in its canonical form (`client.id_hash`), so both of its forms print alike."""
    return id_hash(value)


def _hex32(value: str) -> bool:
    return len(value) == 32 and all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in value)


def _plaud_ids(rec: Recording) -> list[str]:
    return [canonical_plaud_id(s.ref) for s in rec.sources if s.kind == "plaud"]


def _section(cfg: Config, name: str) -> dict:
    value = cfg.data.get(name, {})
    return value if isinstance(value, dict) else {}


def _production(path: Path | None) -> dict:
    """The deployment's own config.toml, read for its `[plaud]` patterns and word only."""
    if path is None:
        raise SpikeRefused(
            "refused before any call: give --production-config (the deployment's config.toml, "
            "$REPO_DIR/config.toml)"
        )
    try:
        return tomllib.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError):
        raise SpikeRefused(
            "refused before any call: the deployment's config.toml (--production-config) can't "
            "be read"
        ) from None


def _word(data: dict, which: str) -> str:
    plaud = data.get("plaud", {})
    word = plaud.get("keep_out_word", DEFAULT_WORD) if isinstance(plaud, dict) else None
    if not valid_word(word):
        raise SpikeRefused(f"refused: configuration: {which} `keep_out_word` is invalid")
    return word


def _enforced_words(cfg: Config) -> list[str]:
    """Every keep-out word the worker has enforced (plaud_state, Task 6's `K_KEEP_OUT_WORDS`), read
    from state.db without writing it: none when `[state] path` is unset or no worker ran yet."""
    state = State.read_only(cfg.state_path) if cfg.state_path is not None else None
    if state is None:
        return []
    try:
        with state.db() as db:
            row = db.execute(
                "SELECT value FROM plaud_state WHERE key = ?", (ENFORCED_WORDS,)
            ).fetchone()
    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
        if isinstance(exc, sqlite3.OperationalError) and "no such table" in str(exc):
            return []
        raise SpikeRefused(
            "refused before any call: state.db can't be read, so the keep-out words the sync "
            f"enforces are unknown ({type(exc).__name__})"
        ) from None
    try:
        words = json.loads(row[0]) if row else []
    except ValueError:
        words = []
    return [w for w in words if valid_word(w)] if isinstance(words, list) else []


def build_guard(cfg: Config, archive: Archive, production: Path | None) -> Guard:
    """The consent list (fail-closed), the archive's private recordings (refused when the path isn't
    the archive or it holds none), and every keep-out word and auto-private pattern the session's
    config, the deployment's config and the worker know, erring towards refusing."""
    try:
        path = consent_list_path(cfg.data)
    except ConsentListError:
        path = None
    consent = read_consent(path)
    if consent.stop is not None:
        raise SpikeRefused(f"refused before any call: {consent.stop}")
    try:
        read_sentinel(archive.root)
    except SentinelError:
        raise SpikeRefused(
            "refused before any call: [archive] path holds no archive.json, so it isn't the "
            "archive (is its disk mounted?), and private ones can't be known"
        ) from None
    recordings = list(archive.iter_recordings())
    if archive.problems:
        raise SpikeRefused(
            f"refused before any call: {len(archive.problems)} recordings in the archive can't "
            "be read, so it can't tell which are private (run `recordings validate`)"
        )
    if not recordings:
        raise SpikeRefused(
            "refused before any call: the archive holds no recordings, so it can't tell which "
            "are private: check [archive] path"
        )
    deployed = _production(production)
    words = [_word(cfg.data, "the session's"), _word(deployed, "the deployment's")]
    words += [*_enforced_words(cfg), DEFAULT_WORD]
    try:
        patterns = (*patterns_from_config(cfg.data), *patterns_from_config(deployed))
    except ConfigError:
        raise SpikeRefused("refused: configuration: `auto_private_patterns` is invalid") from None
    return Guard(
        consent=consent.ids,
        private_ids=frozenset(
            pid for rec in recordings if is_private(rec) for pid in _plaud_ids(rec)
        ),
        here=frozenset(pid for rec in recordings for pid in _plaud_ids(rec)),
        words=tuple(dict.fromkeys(words)),
        patterns=tuple(dict.fromkeys(patterns)),
    )


def _kept_apart(cfg: Config) -> list[Path]:
    """The folders the spike folder stays out of: the archive, the state folder, the index,
    /plaud, and the backup's paths (the archive and the state folder are backed up too)."""
    backup = _section(cfg, "backup")
    named = [backup.get("restore_scratch"), backup.get("cache_dir")]
    extra = backup.get("extra_paths", [])
    named += extra if isinstance(extra, list) else []
    paths = [cfg.archive_path, cfg.state_path, PLAUD_MOUNT]
    paths += [Path(p).expanduser() for p in named if isinstance(p, str) and p]
    if cfg.index_path is not None:
        paths.append(cfg.index_path.parent)
    return [Path(p).expanduser().absolute().resolve() for p in paths if p is not None]


def spike_folder(home: Path) -> Path:
    """`$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike` at 0700, made if missing. Refused when it is wider than 0700, or
    inside (or holding) the archive, the state folder, the index, `/plaud` or a backup path."""
    folder = Path(home).expanduser().absolute() / "spike"
    resolved = folder.resolve()
    for kept in _kept_apart(load_config(os.environ)):
        if resolved.is_relative_to(kept) or kept.is_relative_to(resolved):
            raise SpikeRefused(
                "refused: the spike folder must be outside the archive, the state folder, the "
                f"index, {PLAUD_MOUNT} and every backup path"
            )
    folder.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if stat.S_IMODE(folder.stat().st_mode) & 0o077:
        raise SpikeRefused(f"refused: the spike folder must be 0700: chmod 700 {folder}")
    return folder


class FileTokens:
    """The session's sign-in, read from --token-file: the vendor CLI's token file, whose access
    token audio-router read as "access_token". A spike never refreshes behind Dan's back, so a
    401 is reported as it is."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        self.path = path

    def data(self) -> dict:
        try:
            data = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            raise PlaudAuthError() from None
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise PlaudAuthError()
        return data

    def access_token(self) -> str:
        token = self.data().get("access_token")
        if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
            raise PlaudAuthError()
        return token

    def refresh(self, rejected: str) -> str:
        raise PlaudAuthError()


@dataclass
class Session:
    args: argparse.Namespace
    cfg: Config
    archive: Archive
    guard: Guard
    folder: Path
    tokens: FileTokens
    client: PlaudClient
    monotonic: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic
    now: Callable[[], datetime] = field(default=lambda: datetime.now(UTC))


# -- printing --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def say(*parts: object) -> None:
    print(*parts, flush=True)


def _error(exc: BaseException) -> str:
    return type(exc).__name__


def _yes(value: object) -> str:
    return "yes" if value else "no"


def _names(keys: Iterable[object]) -> str:
    return ", ".join(sorted(str(k) for k in keys)) or "none"


def _code(reply: dict) -> str:
    """The OAuth `error` code, only when it looks like one (never its description)."""
    code = reply.get("error")
    if isinstance(code, str) and 0 < len(code) <= 40 and set(code) <= _CODE_CHARS:
        return f", error {code}"
    return ""


def _time(value: object) -> str:
    """An expiry as a UTC time, from epoch seconds (or milliseconds) or ISO 8601; a smaller number
    is a duration in seconds. Anything else is only "present"."""
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "present"
    if isinstance(value, int | float):
        if value > 10**9:
            seconds = value / 1000 if value > 10**12 else value
            return datetime.fromtimestamp(seconds, UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")
        return f"{int(value)} s"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        try:
            when = datetime.fromisoformat(value)
        except ValueError:
            return "present"
        when = when if when.tzinfo else when.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
        return when.astimezone(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")
    return "present"


def _expires(url: object) -> str:
    """A presigned link's X-Amz-Expires, as seconds, or "unknown"."""
    if not isinstance(url, str):
        return "unknown"
    values = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).query).get("X-Amz-Expires", [])
    return f"{values[0]} s" if values and values[0].isdigit() else "unknown"


# -- reading Plaud ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _batch(payload: Any) -> tuple[str, list]:
    if isinstance(payload, list):
        return "a list", payload
    if isinstance(payload, dict):
        key = next((k for k in _LIST_KEYS if isinstance(payload.get(k), list)), None)
        return f"an object with keys {_names(payload)}", payload[key] if key else []
    return "neither a list nor an object", []


@dataclass
class Listing:
    rows: list[Listed]
    malformed: int
    pages: int

    def census(self) -> str:
        forms = collections.Counter(
            "of_"
            if row.listed_id.lower().startswith("of_")
            else "bare"
            if _hex32(row.listed_id.lower())
            else "other"
            for row in self.rows
        )
        return f"of_ {forms['of_']}, bare {forms['bare']}, other {forms['other']}"

    def by_canonical(self) -> dict[str, Listed]:
        return {row.canonical_id: row for row in self.rows}


def _listing(client: PlaudClient) -> Listing:
    """Every page until an empty one, never stopping at a short one (§11.2)."""
    rows: list[Listed] = []
    malformed = 0
    for page in range(1, PAGE_CAP + 1):
        result = client.list_page(page)
        if not result.rows and not result.malformed:
            return Listing(rows, malformed, page)
        rows += result.rows
        malformed += result.malformed
    raise SpikeRefused(f"stopped: the listing reached {PAGE_CAP} pages, which makes it bad")


def _raw_rows(client: PlaudClient) -> list[dict]:
    """Every listed row as Plaud gave it (S9's listing fields, S12's times), paging alike."""
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for page in range(1, PAGE_CAP + 1):
        _shape, batch = _batch(client.get_json(f"{LIST_PATH}?page={page}&page_size={PAGE_SIZE}"))
        if not batch:
            return rows
        rows += [row for row in batch if isinstance(row, dict)]
    raise SpikeRefused(f"stopped: the listing reached {PAGE_CAP} pages, which makes it bad")


def _files(client: PlaudClient, listed_id: str) -> dict:
    """files/{id}, without fetching the blocks behind links (S7, S9, S11)."""
    env = client.get_json(FILE_PATH.format(urllib.parse.quote(listed_id, safe="")))
    if not isinstance(env, dict):
        raise SpikeRefused("stopped: files/{id} didn't answer an object")
    return env


def _checked(session: Session, row: Listed) -> dict | None:
    """files/{id}, and the guard again on the title the envelope itself gives, before any block or
    download (§11.5: the listing's title alone isn't enough). None, said, when it is refused."""
    env = _files(session.client, row.listed_id)
    title = env.get("name")
    title = title if isinstance(title, str) else None
    if session.guard.allows(row.listed_id, title, own_clip=session.args.own_clip):
        return env
    say(f"{short(row.canonical_id)}: refused by the guard")
    return None


def _resolve(session: Session, given: str) -> str:
    """--id is a Plaud ID, in any form, or an archive recording ID: then its first Plaud ID."""
    if ID_RE.fullmatch(given):
        try:
            ids = _plaud_ids(session.archive.load(given))
        except (KeyError, ValueError):
            ids = []
        if not ids:
            raise SpikeRefused(f"refused: {short(given)} is no recording with a Plaud source")
        return ids[0]
    return canonical_plaud_id(given)


def _named(session: Session, listing: Listing, count: int) -> list[Listed]:
    """The recordings Dan named with --id, as listed, each passed by the guard."""
    if not session.args.id:
        raise SpikeRefused(f"refused: name up to {count} recordings with --id")
    found = listing.by_canonical()
    allowed = []
    for given in session.args.id[:count]:
        canonical = _resolve(session, given)
        row = found.get(canonical)
        if row is None:
            say(f"{short(canonical)}: not listed")
        elif session.guard.allows(row.listed_id, row.title, own_clip=session.args.own_clip):
            allowed.append(row)
        else:
            say(f"{short(canonical)}: refused by the guard")
    return allowed


class _NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        return None


def _post_form(url: str, fields: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[int | None, dict]:
    """One form POST to the token URL, never redirected: the status and the reply's JSON object,
    or (None, {}) when unreachable. Nothing of it is printed here."""
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        url,
        data=urllib.parse.urlencode(fields).encode("ascii"),
        method="POST",
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "Accept": "application/json"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.build_opener(_NoRedirect).open(request, timeout=TIMEOUT) as response:
            status, body = response.status, response.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        status, body = exc.code, exc.read()
        exc.close()
    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError, ValueError):
        return None, {}
    try:
        reply = json.loads(body)
    except ValueError:
        reply = {}
    return status, reply if isinstance(reply, dict) else {}


def _raw_get(url: str, headers: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[int | None, list[str]]:
    """A GET that reads at most one byte, never redirected: the status and the header names."""
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, method="GET", headers=headers)
    try:
        with urllib.request.build_opener(_NoRedirect).open(request, timeout=TIMEOUT) as response:
            response.read(1)
            return response.status, list(response.headers.keys())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        names = list(exc.headers.keys())
        exc.close()
        return exc.code, names
    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError, ValueError):
        return None, []


def _token_url(url: str | None) -> str:
    parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url) if isinstance(url, str) else None
    if parts is None or parts.scheme != "https" or not parts.hostname:
        raise SpikeRefused(
            "refused: --token-url must be the https token URL, from the vendor CLI's own refresh "
            "(runbook 1c)"
        )
    return url


def _refresh_fields(data: dict, refresh_token: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """A refresh's form: the grant, the refresh token, and the token file's `client_id` when it
    has one (S1 prints its key names), as an OAuth client sends it."""
    fields = {"grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": refresh_token}
    client_id = data.get("client_id")
    if isinstance(client_id, str) and client_id:
        fields["client_id"] = client_id
    return fields


def _refused(reply: dict) -> str:
    """What a refused refresh means for the session. An OAuth error code usually means the request
    isn't the one Plaud expects: compare it with the vendor CLI's own refresh first (runbook 1c,
    session A step 3). Only when the two match, and the Mac refreshes while this server is refused,
    is it spec §18's "refused from the server's address"."""
    if _code(reply):
        return (
            "the refresh was refused with an OAuth error code: compare this request with the "
            "vendor CLI's own refresh (runbook 1c, session A step 3) before reading it as the "
            "design failing"
        )
    return "the refresh was refused from this machine: stop and ask Dan"


def _save_tokens(session: Session, data: dict, reply: dict) -> None:
    """Keep the session's sign-in usable after a refresh: the reply's tokens replace the old ones
    in the token file, written atomically at 0600 in the spike folder."""
    new = dict(data)
    for key in ("access_token", "refresh_token", "expires_in", "expires_at", "token_type"):
        if key in reply:
            new[key] = reply[key]
    path = session.tokens.path
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, prefix=".tokens-")  # created at 0600
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(new, fh)
            fh.flush()
            os.fsync(fh.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        Path(tmp).unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise


def _claims(token: object) -> dict | None:
    """A JWT's claims, for their names and times only; None for anything else."""
    if not isinstance(token, str) or token.count(".") != 2:
        return None
    middle = token.split(".")[1]
    try:
        claims = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(middle + "=" * (-len(middle) % 4)))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return claims if isinstance(claims, dict) else None


# -- the spikes ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def s1(session: Session) -> None:
    """The token's shape and lifetime: key names, token type, expiries, a refresh token."""
    try:
        data = session.tokens.data()
    except PlaudAuthError:
        raise SpikeRefused("refused: no readable token file at --token-file") from None
    say(f"token file keys: {_names(data)}")
    kind = data.get("token_type")
    say(f"token type: {kind if isinstance(kind, str) and kind.isalpha() else 'unknown'}")
    say(f"refresh token: {_yes(data.get('refresh_token'))}")
    for key in sorted(data):
        if "expire" in key.lower() or key.lower() in ("exp", "iat", "obtained_at", "created_at"):
            say(f"{key}: {_time(data[key])}")
    for name in ("access_token", "refresh_token"):
        claims = _claims(data.get(name))
        if claims is None:
            say(f"{name}: not a JWT")
            continue
        say(f"{name} claims: {_names(claims)}")
        if isinstance(claims.get("exp"), int | float):
            say(f"{name} expires: {_time(claims['exp'])}")
        if all(isinstance(claims.get(k), int | float) for k in ("exp", "iat")):
            say(f"{name} lifetime: {int(claims['exp'] - claims['iat']) // 60} min")


def s2(session: Session) -> None:
    """Refresh and rotation: one refresh, the old refresh token again, then one listing page."""
    url = _token_url(session.args.token_url)
    data = session.tokens.data()
    old = data.get("refresh_token")
    if not isinstance(old, str) or not old:
        raise SpikeRefused("refused: the sign-in has no refresh token: stop and ask Dan (S1)")
    status, reply = _post_form(url, _refresh_fields(data, old))
    say(f"refresh: HTTP {status}{_code(reply)}")
    if status != 200 or not reply.get("access_token"):
        say(_refused(reply))
        return
    new = reply.get("refresh_token")
    say(f"reply keys: {_names(reply)}")
    say(f"new refresh token: {_yes(new)} · rotated: {_yes(new and new != old)}")
    if "expires_in" in reply:
        say(f"expires_in: {_time(reply['expires_in'])}")
    _save_tokens(session, data, reply)
    again, again_reply = _post_form(url, _refresh_fields(data, old))
    say(f"the old refresh token again: HTTP {again}{_code(again_reply)}")
    if again == 200 and again_reply.get("access_token"):
        _save_tokens(session, session.tokens.data(), again_reply)  # the newest pair is kept
    try:
        page = session.client.list_page(1, 10)
        say(f"one listing page with the new access token: ok, {len(page.rows)} rows")
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"one listing page with the new access token: {_error(exc)}")


def s3(session: Session) -> None:
    """Does a second sign-in sign the first out? One cheap call with the session's sign-in."""
    try:
        session.client.list_page(1, 10)
        say("signed in: yes")
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"signed in: no ({_error(exc)})")


def s4(session: Session) -> None:
    """A refused refresh: a copy of the refresh token with one character changed."""
    url = _token_url(session.args.token_url)
    data = session.tokens.data()
    old = data.get("refresh_token")
    if not isinstance(old, str) or not old:
        raise SpikeRefused("refused: the sign-in has no refresh token: stop and ask Dan (S1)")
    changed = old[:-1] + ("A" if old[-1] != "A" else "B")
    status, reply = _post_form(url, _refresh_fields(data, changed))
    say(f"refused refresh: HTTP {status}{_code(reply)}")


def _pass(client: PlaudClient, n: int) -> set[str]:
    listing = _listing(client)
    ids = [row.canonical_id for row in listing.rows]
    unique = set(ids)
    say(
        f"pass {n}: {len(unique)} IDs, {len(ids) - len(unique)} repeats, {listing.malformed} "
        f"malformed, {listing.pages} pages · census {listing.census()} · "
        f"ID set {short(','.join(sorted(unique)))}"
    )
    return unique


def s5(session: Session) -> None:
    """The listing's shape, a cheap change signal, and paging."""
    for size in SIZES:
        try:
            payload = session.client.get_json(f"{LIST_PATH}?page=1&page_size={size}")
        except PlaudError as exc:
            say(f"page 1 at size {size}: {_error(exc)}")
            continue
        shape, batch = _batch(payload)
        rows = [row for row in batch if isinstance(row, dict)]
        say(f"page 1 at size {size}: {len(batch)} rows, {shape}")
        say(f"  row fields: {_names({key for row in rows for key in row})}")
        for key, value in sorted(payload.items() if isinstance(payload, dict) else []):
            if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool):
                say(f"  {key}: {value}")
    first = _pass(session.client, 1)
    sleep(PAUSE)
    second = _pass(session.client, 2)
    say(
        f"same ID set: {_yes(first == second)} · only in pass 1: {len(first - second)} · "
        f"only in pass 2: {len(second - first)}"
    )


def s7(session: Session) -> None:
    """The ID form: listing IDs against the archive's, the consent list, and three audio hashes.
    The archive is read itself, because the index lives in a Docker volume."""
    listing = _listing(session.client)
    listed = set(listing.by_canonical())
    here = {
        pid: rec.media.sha256
        for rec in session.archive.iter_recordings()
        for pid in _plaud_ids(rec)
    }
    say(f"listed: {len(listed)} · census {listing.census()}")
    say(
        f"in the archive: {len(listed & set(here))} · listed, not in the archive: "
        f"{len(listed - set(here))} · in the archive, not listed: {len(set(here) - listed)}"
    )
    say(f"consent-list IDs in the listing: {len(session.guard.consent & listed)}")
    named = _named(session, listing, 3)
    for row in named:
        name = short(row.canonical_id)
        if row.canonical_id not in here:
            say(f"{name}: not in the archive")
            continue
        dest = session.folder / f"s7-{name}.audio"
        try:
            env = _checked(session, row)
            if env is None:
                continue
            link = check_link(env.get("presigned_url"), api_base=session.client.api_base)
            session.client.download(link, dest)
            say(f"{name}: audio identical: {_yes(sha256_file(dest) == here[row.canonical_id])}")
        except PlaudError as exc:
            say(f"{name}: {_error(exc)}")
        finally:
            dest.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    if named:
        bare = named[0].canonical_id
        for label, form in (("of_ form", f"of_{bare}"), ("bare hex", bare)):
            try:
                _files(session.client, form)
                say(f"files/{{id}} by its {label}: ok")
            except PlaudError as exc:
                say(f"files/{{id}} by its {label}: {_error(exc)}")


def _blocks(env: dict) -> list[dict]:
    blocks = []
    for section in ("source_list", "note_list"):
        value = env.get(section)
        blocks += [b for b in value if isinstance(b, dict)] if isinstance(value, list) else []
    return blocks


def s8(session: Session) -> None:
    """The envelope and volatility: five recordings, each fetched twice, a minute apart."""
    listing = _listing(session.client)
    owners: dict[str, set[str]] = collections.defaultdict(set)  # embeddingKey's hash -> recordings
    for row in _named(session, listing, 5):
        name = short(row.canonical_id)
        try:
            if _checked(session, row) is None:
                continue
            first = session.client.envelope(row.listed_id)
            sleep(PAUSE)
            second = session.client.envelope(row.listed_id)
        except PlaudError as exc:
            say(f"{name}: {_error(exc)}")
            continue
        say(f"{name}: envelope keys: {_names(first)}")
        say(f"{name}: audio link expires in {_expires(first.get('presigned_url'))}")
        for block in _blocks(first):
            kind = block.get("data_type")
            kind = kind if isinstance(kind, str) and kind.isidentifier() else "unknown"
            link, error = block.get("data_link"), block.get("_data_link_error")
            line = f"{name}: block {kind}: keys {_names(block)} · behind a link: {_yes(link)}"
            if link:
                line += f" · link expires in {_expires(link)}"
            if isinstance(error, str) and error.isidentifier():
                line += f" · error {error}"
            say(line)
        rows = transcript_rows(first) or []
        say(f"{name}: segments: {len(rows)}")
        for r in rows:
            if isinstance(r.get("embeddingKey"), str) and r["embeddingKey"]:
                owners[short(r["embeddingKey"])].add(row.canonical_id)
        before, after = part_hashes(first), part_hashes(second)
        for part in sorted(set(before) | set(after)):
            label = "notes" if part.startswith("notes:") else part  # a tab's name is Dan's
            say(f"{name}: part {label}: matched {_yes(before.get(part) == after.get(part))}")
    shared = sum(1 for recordings in owners.values() if len(recordings) > 1)
    say(f"embeddingKey values seen in more than one recording: {shared}")


def _changed(new: dict, old: dict) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(k for k in set(new) | set(old) if new.get(k) != old.get(k))


def _clip(session: Session, listing: Listing, last: dict) -> tuple[str, Listed | None, str | None]:
    """S9's clip, from --id: the 8-hex name the run without --id printed for it, or its Plaud ID.
    Its name, its listed row (None once it isn't listed), and the ID to ask files/{id} by: as
    listed, else as the last run kept it in the spike folder, else as given."""
    given = session.args.id[0]
    if _SHORT.fullmatch(given):
        rows = [row for row in listing.rows if short(row.canonical_id) == given]
        if len(rows) > 1:
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: two listed recordings print that name: give the Plaud ID")
        if rows:
            return given, rows[0], rows[0].listed_id
        kept = last.get("listed_id") if last.get("id") == given else None
        return given, None, kept if isinstance(kept, str) else None
    canonical = _resolve(session, given)
    return short(canonical), listing.by_canonical().get(canonical), given


def s9(session: Session) -> None:
    """What an edit looks like, on Dan's own throwaway clip (session C). Without --id: the newest
    listed rows, for (a), each by the name --id then takes. With --id (and --own-clip): the clip's
    parts and listing fields, and what changed since the last run."""
    listing = _listing(session.client)
    if not session.args.id:
        dated = [row for row in listing.rows if row.recorded_at]
        for row in sorted(dated, key=lambda r: r.recorded_at, reverse=True)[:5]:
            minutes = int((session.now() - row.recorded_at).total_seconds() // 60)
            word = keep_out_match(row.title, session.guard.words) is not None
            say(f"{short(row.canonical_id)}: keep-out word: {_yes(word)} · {minutes} min old")
        return
    record_path = session.folder / "s9-last.json"
    try:
        last = json.loads(record_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        last = {}
    last = last if isinstance(last, dict) else {}
    name, row, ask_by = _clip(session, listing, last)
    canonical = row.canonical_id if row else canonical_plaud_id(ask_by) if ask_by else None
    if session.args.own_clip and canonical in session.guard.here:
        raise SpikeRefused("refused: --own-clip is for a clip that isn't in the archive")
    say(f"{name}: listed: {_yes(row)}")
    if row is None:
        # Its title was checked by the run that recorded it; consent and private are checked now.
        checked = last.get("id") == name and last.get("pattern_ok") is True
        if ask_by is None or not checked or not session.guard.allows(ask_by, "", own_clip=True):
            say(f"{name}: files/{{id}} not fetched: no earlier run checked its title")
            return
        try:
            _files(session.client, ask_by)
            say(f"{name}: files/{{id}}: ok")
        except PlaudError as exc:
            say(f"{name}: files/{{id}}: {_error(exc)}")
        return
    say(f"{name}: keep-out word: {_yes(keep_out_match(row.title, session.guard.words))}")
    if not session.guard.allows(row.listed_id, row.title, own_clip=session.args.own_clip):
        say(f"{name}: refused by the guard")
        return
    if _checked(session, row) is None:
        return
    raw = next(
        (r for r in _raw_rows(session.client) if canonical_plaud_id(str(r.get("id"))) == canonical),
        {},
    )
    try:
        first = session.client.envelope(row.listed_id)
        sleep(MOMENT)
        second = session.client.envelope(row.listed_id)
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"{name}: {_error(exc)}")
        return
    parts = {p: h[:8] for p, h in part_hashes(first).items()}
    again = {p: h[:8] for p, h in part_hashes(second).items()}
    say(f"{name}: parts that differ a moment apart: {_names(_changed(parts, again))}")
    fields = {key: short(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True)) for key, value in raw.items()}
    record = {
        "id": name,
        "listed_id": row.listed_id,  # kept in the 0700 spike folder only, never printed
        "at": session.now().isoformat(),
        "parts": parts,
        "fields": fields,
        "pattern_ok": True,
    }
    if last.get("id") == name:
        seconds = int((session.now() - datetime.fromisoformat(last["at"])).total_seconds())
        say(f"{name}: parts changed since the last run: {_names(_changed(parts, last['parts']))}")
        changed_fields = _names(_changed(fields, last["fields"]))
        say(f"{name}: listing fields changed since the last run: {changed_fields}")
        say(f"{name}: seconds since the last run: {seconds}")
    record_path.write_text(json.dumps(record), encoding="utf-8")
    record_path.chmod(0o600)


def s10(session: Session) -> None:
    """Pacing: twenty calls at one a second, and the rate-limit headers' names. It stops at the
    first 429: a spike never provokes one on purpose."""
    url = f"{session.client.api_base}{LIST_PATH}?page=1&page_size=10"
    limits: set[str] = set()
    statuses: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    for n in range(20):
        auth = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {session.tokens.access_token()}"}
        status, names = _raw_get(url, {**auth, "User-Agent": "recordings-spike"})
        statuses[str(status)] += 1
        limits |= {h for h in names if "ratelimit" in h.lower() or "retry" in h.lower()}
        if status == 429:
            say(f"stopped at call {n + 1}: HTTP 429")
            break
        sleep(1.0)
    say(f"statuses: {', '.join(f'{k} ×{v}' for k, v in sorted(statuses.items()))}")
    retry_after = any(h.lower() == "retry-after" for h in limits)
    say(f"rate-limit headers: {_names(limits)} · Retry-After seen: {_yes(retry_after)}")


def s11(session: Session) -> None:
    """A large download: size, time, throughput, Content-Length, Range, and the link's expiry."""
    named = _named(session, _listing(session.client), 1)
    if not named:
        return
    row = named[0]
    try:
        env = _checked(session, row)
        if env is None:
            return
        link = check_link(env.get("presigned_url"), api_base=session.client.api_base)
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"{short(row.canonical_id)}: {_error(exc)}")
        return
    status, _names_seen = _raw_get(link, {"Range": "bytes=0-0"})
    say(f"Range honoured: {_yes(status == 206)} (HTTP {status})")
    dest = session.folder / "s11.audio"
    start = session.monotonic()
    try:
        size = session.client.download(link, dest)
        seconds = max(session.monotonic() - start, 0.001)
        say(f"size: {size / 1e6:.1f} MB · {seconds:.0f} s · {size / 1e6 / seconds:.2f} MB/s")
        say("Content-Length: present")  # download() refuses a body without one
        expires = _expires(link)
        passed = expires != "unknown" and seconds > float(expires.split()[0])
        say(f"link expires in {expires} · its expiry passed during the download: {_yes(passed)}")
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"download: {_error(exc)}")
    finally:
        dest.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def s12(session: Session) -> None:
    """Time zones: Plaud's start time for three recordings Dan remembers, read both ways."""
    listing = _listing(session.client)
    raw = {canonical_plaud_id(str(r.get("id"))): r for r in _raw_rows(session.client)}
    zone = ZoneInfo(session.cfg.default_timezone)
    for row in _named(session, listing, 3):
        given = raw.get(row.canonical_id, {}).get("start_at")
        if not isinstance(given, str) or row.start_at is None:
            say(f"{short(row.canonical_id)}: no start time")
            continue
        marked = "Z" if given.endswith("Z") else "an offset, or nothing"
        as_utc = row.start_at.astimezone(zone).strftime("%H:%M")
        as_local = row.start_at.replace(tzinfo=None).strftime("%H:%M")
        say(
            f"{short(row.canonical_id)}: marked {marked} · read as UTC, in "
            f"{session.cfg.default_timezone}: {as_utc} · read as local time: {as_local}"
        )


SPIKE_FUNCTIONS: dict[str, Callable[[Session], None]] = {
    "s1": s1,
    "s2": s2,
    "s3": s3,
    "s4": s4,
    "s5": s5,
    "s7": s7,
    "s8": s8,
    "s9": s9,
    "s10": s10,
    "s11": s11,
    "s12": s12,
}


def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="plaud_spike.py", description="stage 2b's spikes (§18)")
    ap.add_argument("spike", choices=SPIKES)
    ap.add_argument(
        "--home",
        default=os.environ.get("RECORDINGS_HOME"),
        help="RECORDINGS_HOME, the spike folder's parent",
    )
    repo = os.environ.get("REPO_DIR")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--production-config",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(repo) / "config.toml" if repo else None,
        help="the deployment's config.toml, for its patterns and word ($REPO_DIR/config.toml)",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--token-file", type=Path, help="the session's token file, in the spike folder")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--id",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        help="a Plaud ID or an archive recording ID (S7, S8, S9, S11, S12); for S9 also the "
        "8-hex name its run without --id printed",
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--token-url", help="S2 and S4: the https token URL, from the vendor CLI's own refresh"
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--own-clip",
        action="store_true",
        help="S9 only, for a clip that isn't in the archive: skip the keep-out check",
    )
    return ap


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)
    guard: Guard | None = None
    try:
        if args.own_clip and args.spike != "s9":
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: --own-clip is for S9 only")
        if args.spike in ("s2", "s4"):
            _token_url(args.token_url)  # before anything is read
        elif args.token_url is not None:
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: --token-url is for S2 and S4 only")
        if not args.home:
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: give --home (RECORDINGS_HOME)")
        cfg = load_config(os.environ)
        if cfg.archive_path is None:
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: no archive is configured, so private ones can't be known")
        archive = Archive(cfg.archive_path)
        guard = build_guard(cfg, archive, args.production_config)
        folder = spike_folder(Path(args.home))
        token_file = (args.token_file or folder / "home" / ".plaud" / "tokens.json").absolute()
        if not token_file.resolve().is_relative_to(folder.resolve()):
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: --token-file must be inside the spike folder")
        tokens = FileTokens(token_file)
        api_base = check_api_base(_section(cfg, "plaud").get("api_base", API_BASE))
        client = PlaudClient(tokens, api_base=api_base)
        SPIKE_FUNCTIONS[args.spike](Session(args, cfg, archive, guard, folder, tokens, client))
        return 0
    except SpikeRefused as exc:
        say(str(exc))
        return EXIT_REFUSED
    except ConfigError as exc:
        say(f"refused: {exc}")
        return EXIT_REFUSED
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"stopped: {_error(exc)}")
        return 1
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001  anything else: its class, never its text or a traceback
        say(f"stopped: {_error(exc)}")
        return 1
    finally:
        if guard is not None:
            say(guard.report())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

Its commands start with neither `make` nor `rc`, as `test_the_spikes_need_nothing_the_build_makes` requires.

In `docs/runbooks/first-run.md`:

**Section 1c:** replace

```text
### 1c. Before stage 2b (not needed for 2a)

The token spike and the ID-form spike (§9.1, §19) both call Plaud. Stage 2a makes no Plaud
calls, so they run before stage 2b's deploy, not now.
```

with

````text
### 1c. Before stage 2b (not needed for 2a)

Stage 2b's spikes (its spec's §18) are the first steps that call Plaud, so none of them runs for
2a. Each is a supervised session with Dan, run with `scripts/plaud_spike.py`, before the stage 2b
work that needs its result: **A**, the sign-in (s1, s2, s4, s3; about 45 minutes); **B**, the data
(s5, s7, s8, s10, s12, s11; about an hour); **C**, an edit on a throwaway clip (s9; about 45
minutes). Read the script before each session, at the commit the session will run. It prints only
counts, yes or no, times, status codes, field names and 8-hex names: never a token, a title,
transcript text or a whole Plaud ID. Before any call it reads the consent list fail-closed, checks
that `[archive] path` is the archive and holds recordings, and gathers every keep-out word and
private pattern it can find; it refuses any consent-listed or private recording, and any title
those match, and checks the envelope's own title again before fetching anything behind it. It ends
by saying how many it refused.

**On the homelab server,** with uv installed for your user (see uv's own installation page,
https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/). The script runs from a clone of its own,
at the commit you read, never from `$REPO_DIR`: that checkout is the deployment's, and the boot
unit starts the containers from it. Use branch `stage-2b`'s commit until stage 2b's first phase is
merged, then `main`'s.
```bash
SPIKE_SRC="$HOME/recordings-spike"           # the spikes' own clone
SPIKE_COMMIT="<commit>"                       # the commit whose script you read
git clone "$(git -C "$REPO_DIR" remote get-url origin)" "$SPIKE_SRC"
git -C "$SPIKE_SRC" switch --detach "$SPIKE_COMMIT"
cd "$SPIKE_SRC" && uv sync --frozen
install -d -m 700 "$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike"
${EDITOR:-vi} "$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike/config.toml"
export RECORDINGS_CONFIG="$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike/config.toml"
```
Each session clones afresh, at the commit it runs. The session's own config uses this server's paths, because the containers'
`/archive`, `/state` and `/consent` don't exist out here: `[archive] path` and `default_timezone`,
`[state] path`, and `[plaud] consent_list` (the list's path on this server). It holds no secret.
The script adds the deployment's own `[plaud] auto_private_patterns` and `keep_out_word` (from
`$REPO_DIR/config.toml`, or `--production-config`) and every word the worker has enforced (from
`state.db`) to whatever this file sets, so nothing there needs copying.

**The session's sign-in,** on the Mac, under a temporary `HOME`, so the Mac's own Plaud sign-ins
are untouched. The token file goes into the spike folder without being printed. `HOMELAB` and
`SRV_HOME` are as section 3 sets them.
```bash
tmphome="$(mktemp -d)" && chmod 700 "$tmphome"
HOME="$tmphome" plaud login
ls -A "$tmphome" "$tmphome/.plaud"
ssh "$HOMELAB" "umask 077 && mkdir -p '$SRV_HOME/spike/home/.plaud' && cat > '$SRV_HOME/spike/home/.plaud/tokens.json'" < "$tmphome/.plaud/tokens.json"
rm -rf "$tmphome"
```
`ls -A` shows file names only. If the CLI wrote its sign-in somewhere else under `$tmphome`, copy
that file instead, to the same place on the server. If it wrote none there at all (it keeps the
sign-in elsewhere, such as the system keychain), stop: that is S1's result, and the token store's
plan (stage 2b spec §10.3) needs a new decision before session A can go on.

**Each spike,** on the homelab server, in that shell, in `$SPIKE_SRC`: `uv run python
scripts/plaud_spike.py s1`, and so on. Exit 78 means the guard refused before any call; it says
why.

**Session A** (s1, s2, s4, s3):
1. Before the session, find the token URL and how the vendor CLI refreshes: its own refresh
   request names the URL, its grant type, whether it sends a `client_id`, its content type and its
   headers. Read them in the CLI's installed code on the Mac, or in `audio-router`'s client (its
   `src/` only), never in a token file. S1 doesn't print the URL.
2. Make the session's sign-in (above), then `s1`. If it finds no refresh token, stop (spec §18).
   If the key names include `client_id`, S2 and S4 send it with each refresh.
3. `s2 --token-url <the token URL>`, then `s4 --token-url <the token URL>`. If S2 says "compare
   this request with the vendor CLI's own refresh", don't read the refusal as the design failing
   yet. Compare the script's request (`_refresh_fields` and `_post_form`: a form POST with
   `grant_type=refresh_token`, the refresh token and any `client_id`,
   `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `Accept: application/json` and urllib's own `User-Agent`)
   with what step 1 found:
   - **They differ:** the script needs a new commit, which Dan reviews; then a fresh session
     sign-in and S2 again. That is not a design failure.
   - **They match:** sign in under a new temporary `HOME` on the Mac
     (`cmphome="$(mktemp -d)" && chmod 700 "$cmphome" && HOME="$cmphome" plaud login`) and let the
     CLI refresh there (its own refresh, or any call once its access token has expired). If the
     Mac refreshes while the server is still refused, that is S2's "refused from the server's
     address": stop and ask Dan. If the Mac is refused too, stop and ask Dan.
4. S3, the baseline first: `s3`, which must say "signed in: yes". S2 replays the old refresh
   token, and a server that detects reuse may sign the session out for that; then make a fresh
   session sign-in and run `s3` again until it says yes, so a sign-out below is the new sign-in's
   doing.
5. Then three sign-ins, each followed by `s3`: Plaud's web app; the Plaud MCP's `login` on the
   Mac; the vendor CLI under another temporary `HOME`
   (`otherhome="$(mktemp -d)" && chmod 700 "$otherhome" && HOME="$otherhome" plaud login`).
   Record which one, if any, makes `s3` say "signed in: no".

**Session B** (s5, s7, s8, s10, s12, s11): a fresh session sign-in, then each spike in that
order. S7, S8, S11 and S12 take one `--id` per recording you name for it (a Plaud ID or an
archive recording ID): none private, none consent-listed.

**Session C** (s9), on a short clip you title on the phone, before it uploads, starting with the
keep-out word, and that isn't private:
1. From the moment the phone transfers it, run `s9` with no `--id` every minute or so. Each row
   it prints is the newest listed, by its 8-hex name, with whether its title starts with the
   keep-out word and how old it is. When the clip shows (the word: yes, a few minutes old), its
   name is the clip's `--id`. Record (a): the minutes from the transfer, and whether the word was
   there in its first listing.
2. `s9 --id <its name> --own-clip`: the baseline. The script keeps what it saw, and the clip's
   ID, in the spike folder. `--own-clip` is refused for a recording that is in the archive.
3. (b) Generate a transcript and a summary, then run it again: whether the title kept the word,
   and how long until the transcript and notes appeared.
4. (c) One edit at a time, each followed by the same `s9 --id <its name> --own-clip`: rename a
   speaker; rename the title, keeping the word; regenerate a note (and run it once more while
   the note is still in progress) and add an in-app note; edit a transcript line; move it to a
   folder; delete it to the trash (the run then says whether it is listed, and what `files/{id}`
   answers) and restore it. Each run prints which parts and listing fields changed, and the
   seconds since the last run.
5. At the end, delete the clip in Plaud.

**At the end of each session,** delete the spike folder, the session's sign-in with it, and the
clone:
```bash
rm -rf "$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike"
rm -rf "$SPIKE_SRC"
```
After session A, on the Mac, also delete the temporary `HOME`s of steps 3 and 5, with the live
sign-ins in them (the session's own was deleted once it was copied):
```bash
rm -rf "$cmphome" "$otherhome"
```

**Results.** After each session, fill in its date, the commit it ran and each outcome. Never a
recording's date, time or duration, a token, a title or an ID.

| Spike | Session, date, commit | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| S1 the token's shape and lifetime | A, | |
| S2 refresh and rotation | A, | |
| S4 a refused refresh | A, | |
| S3 a second sign-in elsewhere | A, | |
| S5 the listing's shape and paging | B, | |
| S7 the ID form | B, | |
| S8 the envelope and volatility | B, | |
| S10 pacing | B, | |
| S12 time zones | B, | |
| S11 a large download | B, | |
| S9 what an edit looks like | C, | |
````

  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_requests (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, request_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    plaud_ids TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', recording_ids TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    select_all INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    state TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- queued | running | done | failed | expired | refused
    queued_at TEXT NOT NULL, started_at TEXT, finished_at TEXT,
    progress TEXT,                           -- JSON {"done", "total"}
    message TEXT,                            -- a §15.6 reply phrase
    result TEXT);                            -- JSON: counts and IDs, never a title
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plaud_requests_by_state ON plaud_requests (state, id);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_listing (
    canonical_plaud_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, listed_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    first_seen TEXT NOT NULL, last_seen TEXT NOT NULL, absent_since TEXT,
    kept_out_at TEXT, kept_out_word TEXT,    -- by a word (§12.2); a late keep-out's too
    rekey_of TEXT,                           -- §11.4 step 6: the absent ID it matched, or '*' for several
    released_at TEXT,                        -- §12.2
    needs_review INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- §11.6
    import_failures INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, next_import_at TEXT, parked_at TEXT,
    title_sha256 TEXT, duration_ms INTEGER, change_marker TEXT);   -- only while its recording is here
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_checks (
    recording_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, last_checked_at TEXT, last_changed_at TEXT, next_check_at TEXT,
    interval_seconds INTEGER, fast_checks_left INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    failures INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, failing_since TEXT,
    settled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, baseline_pending INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    held_removals TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', parked_at TEXT, degraded INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    gone_since TEXT, kept_here_at TEXT);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_check_log (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, at TEXT NOT NULL, recording_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    result TEXT NOT NULL, parts_changed TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    parts_volatile TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', counted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, failure_class TEXT);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plaud_check_log_by_at ON plaud_check_log (at);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_private_checked (
    recording_id TEXT NOT NULL, canonical_plaud_id TEXT NOT NULL, title_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL,
    patterns_version INTEGER NOT NULL, checked_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (recording_id, canonical_plaud_id));
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_events (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, at TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    recording_id TEXT, canonical_plaud_id TEXT,
    detail TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',       -- JSON: parts, a fixed "why"; never a title
    open INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, resolved_at TEXT);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plaud_events_by_at ON plaud_events (at);
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plaud_events_one_flag ON plaud_events (recording_id)
    WHERE open = 1 AND kind IN ('kept-out-late', 'consent-late');
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plaud_events_one_unwritten ON plaud_events (recording_id)
    WHERE open = 1 AND kind = 'private-unwritten';
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL);
  ```
- Produces (`recordings/plaud/checks.py`):

  ```python
  NO_SYNC_YET = "No sync has run yet"
  class NoSyncYet(Exception): ...
  def no_such_table(exc: BaseException) -> bool: ...   # sqlite3.OperationalError "no such table"
  EVENT_KINDS = ("imported", "arrived-private", "updated", "retagged-private", "kept-out-late",
                 "consent-late", "private-unwritten", "kept-here", "gone", "released", "rekeyed")
  FLAG_KINDS = ("kept-out-late", "consent-late")
  BLOCKERS = ("sign-in", "consent", "hold", "breaker", "private-unwritten")
  BLOCKER_PREFIX = "blocker:"
  # plaud_state keys (decision 17)
  K_LAST_GOOD_LISTING = "last_good_listing"; K_HOLD = "hold"; K_BREAKER = "breaker"; K_SIGN_IN = "sign_in"
  K_FAILING = "failing"; K_LAST_PING = "last_ping"; K_LAST_STARTED = "last_started"; K_LAST_ENDED = "last_ended"
  K_LAST_TURN = "last_turn"; K_CATCH_UP_DONE = "catch_up_done_at"; K_KEEP_OUT_WORDS = "keep_out_words"
  K_PATTERNS = "patterns"; K_PATTERNS_PASS = "patterns_pass"; K_FULL = "full_sync"
  K_CONSENT = "consent"   # {"read_at": iso, "count": int, …}: the IDs' count, never the IDs (Task 13 writes it, Tasks 8 and 19 read it)
  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class Marker:
      canonical_plaud_id: str
      title_sha256: str
      patterns_version: int
  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class ListingRow: ...   # one field per plaud_listing column, same names
  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class CheckRow: ...     # one field per plaud_checks column, same names
  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class Event:
      id: int; at: datetime; kind: str; recording_id: str | None; canonical_plaud_id: str | None
      detail: dict; open: bool; resolved_at: datetime | None
  class PlaudDB:
      def __init__(self, state: State) -> None: ...
      # plaud_state (values are JSON)
      def get(self, key: str) -> Any | None: ...
      def put(self, key: str, value: Any, *, now: datetime) -> None: ...
      def put_many(self, values: Mapping[str, Any], *, now: datetime) -> None: ...   # one transaction
      def delete(self, key: str) -> None: ...
      def with_prefix(self, prefix: str) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
      # plaud_listing, by any form of the ID
      def listing(self, plaud_id: str) -> ListingRow | None: ...
      def set_listing(self, plaud_id: str, **fields: Any) -> None: ...   # plaud_listing column names only (ValueError otherwise); a missing row is created with the ID as given, dated by the first time being set (first_seen, last_seen, kept_out_at, parked_at, released_at, next_import_at, absent_since), else ValueError (decision 36). Phase 2's listing writes rows; a test seeds a listed one with set_listing(id, last_seen=t)
      # plaud_checks
      def check_row(self, recording_id: str) -> CheckRow | None: ...
      def set_check(self, recording_id: str, **fields: Any) -> None: ...
      # plaud_events
      def add_event(self, kind: str, *, now: datetime, recording_id: str | None = None, plaud_id: str | None = None,
                    detail: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, open_flag: bool = False) -> int: ...
      def open_flags(self, kinds: Iterable[str] = FLAG_KINDS) -> list[Event]: ...
      def resolve(self, event_id: int, *, now: datetime) -> None: ...
      def change_kind(self, event_id: int, kind: str) -> None: ...
      def events_since(self, since: datetime, kinds: Iterable[str]) -> list[Event]: ...
      # plaud_private_checked
      def markers(self, recording_id: str) -> dict[str, Marker]: ...
      def set_markers(self, recording_id: str, markers: Iterable[Marker], *, now: datetime) -> None: ...
      def prune(self, *, now: datetime) -> None: ...   # check log 7 days; events 90 days, open flags kept
  ```
  Every reader raises `NoSyncYet` instead of `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table`.
- Produces (`recordings/plaud/when.py`, standard library only, no sqlite3, so Pyodide imports it):
  ```python
  def parse_stamp(value: object) -> datetime | None: ...   # an ISO string, or a datetime, as an aware datetime; a naive one is UTC; None or junk gives None, never an exception
  def local_hhmm(dt: datetime, tz: tzinfo) -> str: ...     # "14:20" in tz; a naive dt is UTC
  ```
  Tasks 8 (`commands`), 11 (`health`), 13 (`worker`), 14 (`requests`) and 19 (the views) read and show stamps through these instead of their own copies; 2a's `ops.when_label` stays.
- `Index.wal(*, timeout: float = 5.0) -> bool`: switches the file to WAL (a no-op once it is); on `sqlite3.OperationalError` (another process has the file open) it logs "index.db stays in rollback-journal mode for now (<class>)" and returns False. `Index.rebuild` calls it after its commit; `Writer.__init__` calls it on an index it finds this archive's and doesn't rebuild (the one stage 2a deployed), so `index.db` is WAL after the first start of the new release.
- `State.forget(file)`: also deletes the recording's `plaud_checks`, `plaud_private_checked` and `plaud_events` rows, and clears `title_sha256`, `duration_ms` and `change_marker` on the `plaud_listing` rows of its canonical IDs (read from `plaud_private_checked` before deleting).

```python
"""Stage 2b's tables in state.db (2b spec §9.5): tables only, keyed by canonical Plaud ID, read
through PlaudDB. Every ID here is synthetic."""

import sqlite3
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

import pytest
from recordings.init import init_archive
from recordings.plaud.checks import (
    NO_SYNC_YET,
    Marker,
    NoSyncYet,
    PlaudDB,
    no_such_table,
)
from recordings.state import MIGRATIONS, SCHEMA, SCHEMA_VERSION, State

NOW = datetime(2026, 10, 23, 14, 20, tzinfo=UTC)
HEX = f"{0x3FA9:032x}"
OTHER = f"{0xB0B:032x}"
REC = "20261006T140003-0700_3fa91c2e"
REC2 = "20261007T090000-0700_0badc0de"
PLAUD_TABLES = (
    "plaud_requests",
    "plaud_listing",
    "plaud_checks",
    "plaud_check_log",
    "plaud_private_checked",
    "plaud_events",
    "plaud_state",
)
TWO_A_SCHEMA = SCHEMA.split("-- Stage 2b's tables")[0]


@pytest.fixture
def state(tmp_path) -> State:
    init_archive(tmp_path / "archive", tmp_path / "state", writer_id="test")
    return State.open(tmp_path / "state")


def _tables(state: State) -> set[str]:
    with state.db() as db:
        return {r[0] for r in db.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table'")}


def _as_2a(state: State) -> None:
    """Make this state.db what a 2a release left: its tables, none of 2b's."""
    with state.db() as db:
        for table in PLAUD_TABLES:
            db.execute(f"DROP TABLE {table}")


def test_schema_version_stays_1_and_migrations_stay_empty():
    # why: C8.01, §17.3. A version bump or a migration makes an older release refuse this
    # state.db, and `make rollback` to the 2a tag would stop working. 2b adds tables only.
    assert SCHEMA_VERSION == 1
    assert MIGRATIONS == {}


def test_a_2a_state_db_gains_the_2b_tables_on_open(state):
    _as_2a(state)
    started = datetime(2026, 10, 9, 8, 0, tzinfo=UTC)
    state.record_run("backup", started, started, True, "ok")
    revision = state.adopt("recordings/2026/10/x/recording.json", 1, "a" * 64, b"{}")
    assert not _tables(state) & set(PLAUD_TABLES)
    reopened = State.open(state.path)
    assert set(PLAUD_TABLES) <= _tables(reopened)
    assert reopened.last_run("backup").detail == "ok"
    assert reopened.last_committed("recordings/2026/10/x/recording.json").id == revision
    assert reopened.meta("schema_version") == "1"


def test_a_state_db_with_the_2b_tables_still_reads_as_2a_did(state):
    # why: §17.3. An older release opens this file with its own SCHEMA, then reads 2a's tables;
    # the 2b tables must neither break that script nor its reads.
    started = datetime(2026, 10, 9, 8, 0, tzinfo=UTC)
    state.record_run("mirror", started, started, False, "error: `OSError`")
    PlaudDB(state).put("catch_up_done_at", NOW.isoformat(), now=NOW)
    with state.db() as db:
        db.executescript(TWO_A_SCHEMA)  # what a 2a release runs at every open
    reader = State.read_only(state.path)
    assert reader.last_run("mirror", ok=False).detail == "error: `OSError`"
    assert reader.meta("writer_id") == "test" and reader.flags() == []
    assert PlaudDB(reader).get("catch_up_done_at") == NOW.isoformat()


def test_listing_rows_follow_the_canonical_id_across_a_form_flip(state):
    # why: C5.33. Plaud changed its IDs' form once already; a change of form must carry every
    # state over, or a kept-out recording would download and a review mark vanish.
    db = PlaudDB(state)
    db.set_listing("of_" + HEX, kept_out_at=NOW, kept_out_word="noarchive", needs_review=True)
    first = db.listing(HEX)
    assert (first.canonical_plaud_id, first.listed_id, first.first_seen) == (HEX, "of_" + HEX, NOW)
    flag = db.add_event(
        "consent-late", now=NOW, recording_id=REC, plaud_id="OF_" + HEX.upper(), open_flag=True
    )
    later = NOW + timedelta(hours=1)
    db.set_listing(HEX.upper(), listed_id=HEX.upper(), last_seen=later)  # now listed bare
    row = db.listing("of_" + HEX)
    assert row.canonical_plaud_id == HEX and row.listed_id == HEX.upper()
    assert (row.first_seen, row.last_seen) == (NOW, later)
    assert (row.kept_out_at, row.kept_out_word, row.needs_review) == (NOW, "noarchive", True)
    assert db.listing(HEX) == row
    (open_flag,) = db.open_flags()
    assert (open_flag.id, open_flag.canonical_plaud_id) == (flag, HEX)
    with state.db() as conn:
        assert conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM plaud_listing").fetchone()[0] == 1


def test_set_listing_and_set_check_take_column_names_only(state):
    db = PlaudDB(state)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not a settable column: title"):
        db.set_listing(HEX, title="Week 4")  # a listing row never holds a title
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="canonical_plaud_id"):
        db.set_listing(HEX, canonical_plaud_id=OTHER)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="no time to date"):
        db.set_listing(HEX, kept_out_word="noarchive")
    db.set_listing("of_" + HEX, kept_out_at=NOW, kept_out_word="noarchive")  # never listed yet
    row = db.listing(HEX)
    assert (row.listed_id, row.first_seen, row.kept_out_word) == ("of_" + HEX, NOW, "noarchive")
    db.set_listing(OTHER, last_seen=NOW)  # a row dated by the listing that showed it
    assert (db.listing(OTHER).first_seen, db.listing(OTHER).last_seen) == (NOW, NOW)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not a settable column: oops"):
        db.set_check(REC, oops=1)
    db.set_check(REC, failures=2, held_removals=[{"part": "speakers"}], settled=True)
    db.set_check(REC, failures=3)
    check = db.check_row(REC)
    assert (check.failures, check.settled, check.held_removals) == (
        3,
        True,
        ({"part": "speakers"},),
    )
    assert db.check_row(REC2) is None
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="not an event kind"):
        db.add_event("renamed", now=NOW)


def test_one_open_privacy_flag_per_recording(state):
    # why: P15. A recording has one privacy flag, changed in place, never a second.
    db = PlaudDB(state)
    first = db.add_event("kept-out-late", now=NOW, recording_id=REC, open_flag=True)
    for kind in ("consent-late", "kept-out-late"):
        with pytest.raises(sqlite3.IntegrityError):
            db.add_event(kind, now=NOW, recording_id=REC, open_flag=True)
    db.add_event("private-unwritten", now=NOW, recording_id=REC, open_flag=True)  # its own index
    with pytest.raises(sqlite3.IntegrityError):
        db.add_event("private-unwritten", now=NOW, recording_id=REC, open_flag=True)
    db.add_event("consent-late", now=NOW, recording_id=REC2, open_flag=True)  # another recording
    db.add_event("consent-late", now=NOW, recording_id=REC)  # closed events: any number
    db.change_kind(first, "consent-late")
    assert [e.kind for e in db.open_flags() if e.recording_id == REC] == ["consent-late"]
    db.resolve(first, now=NOW)
    db.add_event("kept-out-late", now=NOW, recording_id=REC, open_flag=True)
    assert len(db.open_flags()) == 2


def test_reading_a_missing_2b_table_raises_no_sync_yet(state):
    # why: §9.5. A 2a state.db read by a 2b Status says "No sync has run yet", never the
    # "restore state.db" text that any DatabaseError shows today.
    _as_2a(state)
    db = PlaudDB(State.read_only(state.path))
    for read in (
        lambda: db.get("last_turn"),
        db.open_flags,
        lambda: db.listing(HEX),
        lambda: db.check_row(REC),
        lambda: db.markers(REC),
        lambda: db.events_since(NOW, ["imported"]),
        lambda: db.with_prefix("blocker:"),
    ):
        with pytest.raises(NoSyncYet, match=NO_SYNC_YET):
            read()
    assert no_such_table(sqlite3.OperationalError("no such table: plaud_state"))
    assert not no_such_table(sqlite3.OperationalError("database is locked"))
    assert not no_such_table(ValueError("no such table"))


def test_forget_takes_the_recordings_plaud_rows_and_title_hash(state):
    # why: §9.5. A title hash is kept only while its recording is here; reindex --allow-missing
    # (State.forget) takes it, and the recording's own Plaud rows, with the recording.
    db = PlaudDB(state)
    for rec, ids in ((REC, (HEX, "of_" + OTHER)), (REC2, (f"{7:032x}",))):
        db.set_markers(rec, [Marker(i, "b" * 64, 1) for i in ids], now=NOW)
        for i in ids:
            db.set_listing(
                i, last_seen=NOW, title_sha256="b" * 64, duration_ms=2600, change_marker="m1"
            )
        db.set_check(rec, failures=1)
        db.add_event("imported", now=NOW, recording_id=rec, plaud_id=ids[0])
    db.set_listing(HEX, kept_out_at=NOW, kept_out_word="noarchive")
    state.forget(f"recordings/2026/10/{REC}/recording.json")
    assert db.markers(REC) == {} and db.check_row(REC) is None
    assert db.events_since(NOW - timedelta(days=1), ["imported"])[0].recording_id == REC2
    for i in (HEX, OTHER):
        row = db.listing(i)
        assert (row.title_sha256, row.duration_ms, row.change_marker) == (None, None, None)
    assert db.listing(HEX).kept_out_word == "noarchive"  # kept-out state stays, by Plaud ID
    assert db.listing(f"{7:032x}").title_sha256 == "b" * 64
    assert set(db.markers(REC2)) == {f"{7:032x}"} and db.check_row(REC2).failures == 1


def test_prune_keeps_open_flags_and_drops_old_rows(state):
    db = PlaudDB(state)
    with state.db() as conn:  # phase 3's checks write the log; here it is written by hand
        for days in (8, 6):
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO plaud_check_log (at, recording_id, result) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, 'up to date')",
                ((NOW - timedelta(days=days)).isoformat(), REC),
            )
    old_closed = db.add_event("imported", now=NOW - timedelta(days=91), recording_id=REC)
    old_open = db.add_event(
        "consent-late", now=NOW - timedelta(days=120), recording_id=REC, open_flag=True
    )
    recent = db.add_event("updated", now=NOW - timedelta(days=89), recording_id=REC2)
    db.prune(now=NOW)
    with state.db() as conn:
        assert conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM plaud_check_log").fetchone()[0] == 1
        ids = {r[0] for r in conn.execute("SELECT id FROM plaud_events")}
    assert ids == {old_open, recent} and old_closed not in ids


def test_put_many_is_one_transaction(state):
    db = PlaudDB(state)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        db.put_many({"catch_up_done_at": NOW.isoformat(), "last_turn": object()}, now=NOW)
    assert db.get("catch_up_done_at") is None and db.get("last_turn") is None
    db.put_many({"catch_up_done_at": "x", "blocker:consent": {"since": "y"}}, now=NOW)
    db.put("blocker:hold", {"since": "z"}, now=NOW)
    assert db.with_prefix("blocker:") == {
        "blocker:consent": {"since": "y"},
        "blocker:hold": {"since": "z"},
    }
    db.delete("blocker:hold")
    assert db.get("blocker:hold") is None and db.get("catch_up_done_at") == "x"
```

```python
"""One time parser and one local "HH:MM" for the Plaud sync (`plaud/when.py`): every reader reads
a stored stamp the same way. Every time here is invented."""

import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pytest
from recordings.plaud.when import local_hhmm, parse_stamp

VANCOUVER = ZoneInfo("America/Vancouver")
T = datetime(2026, 10, 23, 21, 20, tzinfo=UTC)


def test_an_iso_stamp_reads_as_an_aware_datetime_and_a_naive_one_as_utc():
    # why: the plan council's M6. Sync health read a naive stamp as UTC and the worker read it as
    # missing, so the schedule and Status could disagree about one last_started. One rule now.
    assert parse_stamp("2026-10-23T21:20:00+00:00") == T
    assert parse_stamp("2026-10-23T21:20:00") == T
    offset = parse_stamp("2026-10-23T14:20:00-07:00")
    assert offset == T and offset.utcoffset() == timedelta(hours=-7)
    assert parse_stamp(T.replace(tzinfo=None)) == T  # a stored datetime, naive
    assert parse_stamp(T) is T


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "junk", [None, "", "yesterday", "2026-13-40T00:00:00", 7, 1.5, True, [], {}]
)
def test_none_or_junk_reads_as_none(junk):
    assert parse_stamp(junk) is None


def test_local_hhmm_is_the_time_in_the_zone_given():
    assert local_hhmm(T, VANCOUVER) == "14:20"
    assert local_hhmm(T, ZoneInfo("Asia/Kolkata")) == "02:50"  # +05:30, the next day
    assert local_hhmm(T.replace(tzinfo=None), VANCOUVER) == "14:20"  # naive: UTC
    assert local_hhmm(T, UTC) == "21:20"


def test_it_needs_the_standard_library_only():
    # why: the Pages demo runs on Pyodide, and the views read their times through this module.
    code = "import sys, recordings.plaud.when; print('sqlite3' in sys.modules)"
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    assert out.stdout.strip() == "False"
```

```text
def test_index_db_is_in_wal_mode(new_archive, tmp_path):
    # why: 2b spec §9.5 (2a rulings, item 72d). web and the worker each hold a Writer: in WAL mode
    # one upserts or rebuilds while the other reads, instead of waiting on a whole-file lock.
    root, _ = new_archive
    rec = put(root)
    index = Index(tmp_path / "index" / "index.db")
    index.rebuild(Archive(root), archive_uuid="u-1")
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(index.path)) as conn:
        assert conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode").fetchone()[0] == "wal"
    index.upsert(rec)  # a later writer's connection keeps the mode the file holds
    assert index.find_by_sha256(rec.media.sha256) == rec.id


def test_a_writer_switches_this_archives_index_to_wal(writer):
    # why: the plan council's R6 and BA1. A Writer rebuilds only a new, damaged or foreign index,
    # so the valid index a 2a deploy left, in rollback-journal mode, would have stayed so: a Writer
    # that finds the index this archive's switches it.
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(writer.index.path)) as conn:
        conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE")  # as stage 2a left it
    Writer(writer.root, writer.state, Index(writer.index.path), writer_id="test")
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(writer.index.path)) as conn:
        assert conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode").fetchone()[0] == "wal"


def test_a_switch_to_wal_that_cant_happen_now_is_logged_and_tried_again(
    new_archive, tmp_path, caplog
):
    # why: the plan council's BA5. The switch needs the file to itself, so it fails while another
    # process reads it (web, as the worker starts). WAL only speeds things up: the rebuild or the
    # Writer carries on, a fixed phrase is logged, and the next one tries again.
    root, _ = new_archive
    put(root)
    index = Index(tmp_path / "index" / "index.db")
    index.rebuild(Archive(root), archive_uuid="u-1")
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(index.path)) as conn:
        conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE")
    reader = sqlite3.connect(index.path)
    try:
        reader.execute("BEGIN")
        reader.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM recordings").fetchone()  # a read in progress
        with caplog.at_level("WARNING", logger="recordings.index"):
            assert index.wal(timeout=0.05) is False
    finally:
        reader.close()
    assert "index.db stays in rollback-journal mode for now (OperationalError)" in caplog.text
    assert index.wal() is True
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(index.path)) as conn:
        assert conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode").fetchone()[0] == "wal"


def test_a_missing_index_answers_nothing(tmp_path):
```

```text
    def forget(self, file: str) -> None:
        """Drop everything state.db remembers about a file that was removed on purpose: its
        revisions and flags, and its recording's Plaud rows (2b spec §9.5): its checks, markers
        and events, and the title hash, duration and change marker on the listing rows of its
        Plaud IDs, which are kept only while it is here. Its other listing state (kept out,
        released, parked) stays, keyed by the Plaud ID."""
        recording_id = PurePosixPath(file).parent.name
        with self.db() as db:
            db.execute("DELETE FROM revisions WHERE file = ?", (file,))
            db.execute("DELETE FROM flags WHERE file = ?", (file,))
            plaud_ids = db.execute(
                "SELECT canonical_plaud_id FROM plaud_private_checked WHERE recording_id = ?",
                (recording_id,),
            ).fetchall()
            db.executemany(
                "UPDATE plaud_listing SET title_sha256 = NULL, duration_ms = NULL, "
                "change_marker = NULL WHERE canonical_plaud_id = ?",
                plaud_ids,

                db.execute(f"DELETE FROM {table} WHERE recording_id = ?", (recording_id,))
```
